A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E. lathyis is a promising plant species for the production of triterpenoids.
the MVA pathway is mainly used by E. lathyis latex to produce triterpenes whereas the MEP pathway is used to synthesize phytosterols.
the latex of E. lathyri contains a mixture of compounds with a complex origin, including the contribution of an endophytic fungi.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MVA pathway is responsible for the synthesis of latex triterpenoids, whereas the synthesis of other isoprenoid compounds (e.g., phytosterols, carotenoids, phytol, etc.) is mainly carried out by the MEP pathway.
the latex is the only tissue in which triterpene biosynthesis occurs via the MVA pathway.
